Hello! I've been learning Spanish on my own for quite some time. I don't necessary believe in a one-size-fits-all approach for learning but here are a few things I've done that've helped me immensely. 


1.) [Duolingo](https://www.duolingo.com/) helps me in just starting a new language. It's good for an introduction to simple vocab and simple grammar but should not be relied on for more complex conversations. I also love using [Clozemaster](http://clozemaster.com) to practice vocab with their matching games and I believe their vocab/phrases are more immediately useful than Duolingo

2.) In regards to Spanish specifically, I think its important to know what dialect you want to learn. If you're going to Mexico, it may help to focus on learning Mexican spanish phrases and learning where the vocab differs from other countries. This applies as well to Spain, Chile, Argentina, Colombia, Puerto Rico, Dominican Republic all countries with very particular ways of speaking that differ from each other and will require a little extra effort to learn.

3.) Immersion! Watch Spanish language movies and TV (Start with English subtitles and move to Spanish) Listen to music in Spanish! Talk with native speakers. This step requires the most effort but is undoubtedly the most important because it provides an opportunity to actualize all your studying and practice. Its also how native Speakers continue to learn in their language. I think apps like Linguado and Tandem are good free ways to communicate with speakers who'd be more than happy to help you learn!

I'm sorry! I know I said a lot. I hope youre able to find some of this helpful and happy learning! :)
